1.title: Pull out the wall wires
1.say: Pull the two black and two white wall wires out of the wall box. Twist the orange caps off clockwise. Leave the copper tips bare and sticking out.
placements: two black wall wires → pulled out to hang right of gray wall box in white wall with about one centimetre bare copper showing, in the video: right side of box
two white wall wires → pulled out to hang right of gray wall box with bare copper showing, in the video: middle and lower right of box
two orange twist caps → twisted off clockwise and set aside off the wires, in the video: removed from top and middle wires
bare ground twists → pushed to back bottom inside gray wall box, in the video: tucked low inside box
watch_for: if an orange cap is still on a wire you missed one and a live end can hide
if the bare copper is shorter than a fingernail pull more wire out so the next cap can grip
1.check_yourself: It should look like four bare copper tips sticking out of the gray wall box with no caps on.
1.safety: Switch the heater power off at the breaker box and keep it off.

2.title: Check the wires have no power
2.say: Touch the red and black tester probes to each pair of bare tips. Check the yellow tester stays dark for every pair.
placements: yellow tester with red probe and black probe → red probe tip touched to one bare copper tip and black probe tip touched to another bare copper tip inside gray wall box tested pair by pair, in the video: probes touch lower twisted copper at bottom right of box
watch_for: if you test only one pair a live wire can hide so test every pairing
if the metal probe tips touch each other the reading can mislead so keep them on the wires only
2.check_yourself: It should look like the red and black tester tips touching the bare wires with the yellow tester dark.
2.safety: Keep your fingers on the plastic handles only and touch no bare metal.

3.title: Twist white wires together
3.say: Hold the two white wall wires together with copper tips even. Twist the yellow cap on clockwise until tight. Push the joined wires to the back of the wall box.
placements: two white wall wires with copper tips even → twisted copper to copper together inside gray wall box, in the video: left white and right white joined in middle of box
yellow twist cap → twisted clockwise over joined white copper tips until tight with no copper showing then pushed to back bottom of gray wall box, in the video: yellow cap tucked low inside box
watch_for: if white copper shows below the yellow cap it can touch the box so twist further until covered
if the cap spins loose the wires are not gripped so pull off and retwist tighter
3.check_yourself: It should look like the two white wires hidden under a yellow cap inside the box with two black wires sticking out.
3.safety: Keep the breaker off and do not touch bare copper while twisting.

4.title: Connect one black wire pair
4.say: Hold one short black wire from the thermostat next to one black wall wire. Twist the red cap on clockwise until no copper shows. Let the thermostat hang down from the joined wires.
placements: one short black wire from hanging black thermostat base → tip held even with tip of one black wall wire from top of gray wall box copper to copper, in the video: left black wall wire at top center
red twist cap → twisted clockwise over both copper tips until tight with no copper showing with thermostat left hanging down, in the video: red cap just above top of box
watch_for: if copper shows below the red cap it can short so twist further until covered
if you grabbed both black wall wires together you have the wrong pair so use only one wall wire
4.check_yourself: It should look like one black wall wire joined under a red cap to the hanging thermostat with the other black wire still free.
4.safety: Keep the power off and touch only the covered wire parts.

5.title: Connect the other black pair
5.say: Hold the last short black thermostat wire against the last black wall wire. Twist the bare copper ends together clockwise until tight.
placements: last short black wire from hanging black thermostat base → tip held even with tip of last black wall wire from top right of gray wall box and twisted copper to copper clockwise until tight, in the video: bare twisted joint sticking up top right above box
watch_for: if you mix the free black wall wire with the white joint the heater will not work so use black to black only
if the twist feels loose and pulls apart the copper was not even so untwist and start even
5.check_yourself: It should look like the black thermostat hangs from the box with one red capped joint and the other black ends twisted together at the top right.
5.safety: Keep the power off and keep the bare ends apart until twisted.

6.title: Screw thermostat to wall
6.say: Push the wires and caps into the wall box. Hold the black thermostat base flat over the wall opening. Drive the top and bottom silver screws into the wall box with the drill.
placements: joined wires with yellow and red caps → folded and pushed inside gray wall box behind base, in the video: tucked to top and back of box
black rectangular base with white center knob → held centered flat over rectangular wall opening on white wall with knob facing out, in the video: centered over opening

top and bottom silver screws → driven with drill driver through top and bottom holes of black base into top and bottom screw holes of gray wall box until flat and straight, in the video: top and bottom center screws
watch_for: if the base rocks or gaps the wires are trapped behind so push wires deeper and retighten
if the base is crooked the cover will sit crooked so loosen and straighten before final tightening
6.check_yourself: It should look like the black base with white knob screwed flat over the wall opening.
6.safety: Keep fingers clear of the spinning drill tip while driving screws.

7.title: Push on the white cover
7.say: Line up the white square cover over the black base. Push it straight in until it clicks.
placements: white square plastic cover with round center dial → lined up over black base on white wall and pushed straight in until flush and centered, in the video: white Honeywell cover centered on white wall with dial marks showing
watch_for: if the cover stands off on one side a corner is caught so pull off and push straight again
if the dial will not turn the cover is not seated centered so lift and reseat
7.check_yourself: It should look like a white square cover with round dial sitting centered on the white wall.
